description: Learn how to change cursor size in macOS and adjust the font size in the Cursor IDE. Follow our step-by-step guide to improve your coding visibility.
intro: To change the cursor size in Cursor on Mac, you must adjust the system-wide pointer settings in your macOS System Settings. To increase the text size within the Cursor IDE, you can modify the internal editor font settings or use the global interface zoom shortcuts.
tldr: Change the system-wide mouse pointer size via macOS System Settings.
Use Cmd + + or Cmd + - to zoom the entire Cursor interface.
Adjust specific editor font sizes in Cursor Settings under Appearance.
Enable Shake mouse pointer to locate for better visibility.

blocks.text: Why adjust your cursor and font settings

High-resolution displays make text sharp but can also make UI elements appear tiny. If you find yourself squinting at your code, you are not alone. Cursor is built on the VS Code architecture, which means it shares many of the same customization capabilities. However, the mouse pointer itself is managed by macOS, not the editor. Understanding this distinction saves time when you try to customize your workspace.
How to change the mouse pointer size on macOS

Your mouse pointer is part of the macOS accessibility suite. Changing it here affects every application you open, including Cursor. This is the most effective way to ensure your pointer is visible against dark or light code themes.

items: Click the Apple Menu () in the top left corner.
Select System Settings from the menu.
Select Display from the list of options.
Move the Pointer size slider to your preferred level.

blocks.text: You do not need to restart your Mac for these changes to take effect. If you still have trouble finding your cursor, you should toggle on the Shake mouse pointer to locate feature. When active, a quick flick of your mouse or trackpad makes the pointer enlarge momentarily, acting like a beacon on your screen.
Adjusting font size inside the Cursor IDE

If the mouse pointer is fine but the code is too small, you need to adjust the editor settings. Cursor allows you to set specific font sizes for the editor and the integrated terminal. These settings are independent of the system-wide zoom.

items: Open Cursor and press Cmd + , to open the Settings menu.
Navigate to the Appearance section in the left sidebar.
Find the Editor: Font Size field.
Enter your desired size in pixels.
Press Enter to confirm the change.

blocks.text: If you use the integrated terminal frequently, you should also look for the Terminal > Integrated: Font Size setting in the same menu. Increasing this value ensures that your console output remains readable during debugging sessions.
Using global zoom for the Cursor interface

Sometimes changing the font size is not enough. You might want the sidebar, the file explorer, and the AI chat panel to be larger as well. Global zoom is the fastest way to achieve this. It treats the entire Cursor window like a web page.

items: Press Cmd + = to zoom in on the entire interface.
Press Cmd + - to zoom out if elements become too large.
Press Cmd + 0 to reset the zoom to the default 100 percent.

blocks.text: This is a great workaround for the AI chat panel. If the text inside the chat bubbles is too small, a single zoom-in step often makes it perfectly legible. Remember that this scales everything, so your file tree and menu bars will also grow.

blocks.text: If you find that your settings are not saving, check your sync settings. If you have multiple devices, your settings might be overwriting each other. You can disable settings sync in the Accounts menu if you want each machine to have its own unique font and size configuration.

faq.question: Does Cursor have a specific setting for mouse pointer size?
faq.answer: No, Cursor does not have a dedicated mouse pointer setting. You must change the pointer size in the macOS Accessibility System Settings.

faq.question: How do I make the chat panel text larger?
faq.answer: There is no individual setting for the chat panel text. Use the Cmd + = keyboard shortcut to zoom the entire Cursor interface.

faq.question: Is Cursor a web app?
faq.answer: No, Cursor is a desktop-native IDE that you install on your Mac. It is not a web app, though it uses web-based technologies for its interface.
